text:
maria: Quick sync — I pushed a prototype GH workflow to auto-capture lightweight nsys traces in nightly perf CI. Goal: catch kernel-selection / batching regressions early.

alex: Nice. Is it full nsys capture or sampled? full traces blow up.

maria: Sampling + selective capture. We record 5 short runs per model (10s each) with `--sample=interval` and only capture kernel timelines + nvtx ranges. Kept output to ~15MB/run on gpu64.

jamal: Can you paste the command you used? want to try on my local nightly branch.

maria: Sure:```bash
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=timer --sample-interval=1000000 \
  --output=/tmp/trace_${GITHUB_RUN_ID} \
  --force-overwrite --quiet -- python -u run_perf_probe.py --model gpt-small --seq 1024 --batch 8
```

alex: Nice. Where do artifacts land? S3 path? retention?

maria: Upload step writes to s3://redwood-ci/perf-traces/${short_sha}/${run_ts}/trace.nsight.zip. 90d retention by default. We also push a tiny JSON metadata blob with sample stats (kernel top10, host time, total tokens).

perf-bot: [upload complete] trace 1755017890-2026-03-01 uploaded -> s3://redwood-ci/perf-traces/sha1234/20260301/trace.nsight.zip :white_check_mark:

jamal: How do we diff traces? existing dashboards need per-kernel delta and flamegraph diffs.

maria: Proto diff pipeline: unpack traces, run a headless parser that extracts kernel name, elapsed_us, cuda-stream, kernel-mem, and produces per-kernel histograms + timeline snippets. Then we compute median+p95 deltas and surface results in the diff dashboard.

sophie: Can we gate on regressions? e.g., if median of top-k kernels increases > 10% block merge.

maria: Yep — we added two gates: (1) threshold rule (top-5 median > baseline * 1.10) and (2) new-kernel alert if a previously unseen kernel shows >1% total time. Both are optional for PRs, required for nightly -> regression pipeline.

alex: What about KV cache behavior? traces need to isolate kv-cache hits vs miss paths so we don't confuse kernel regression with access pattern changes.

maria: We emit NVTX spans around KV read/write ops in the runtime: `NVTX_RANGE_PUSH(\"kv:read:hit\")` / `kv:read:miss`. Parser tags kernel samples with nearest nvtx span to attribute time to cache-hit vs miss. Works well in smoke runs.

jamal: Any perf impact from NVTX? minimal?

maria: Negligible for these short sample runs. For long production runs we'd keep it off.

perf-bot: [diff report] nightly 20260301 vs baseline(20260225) -> top-3 kernel median deltas: AddBiasFwd +7%, SoftmaxKernel +2%, MatMulSplit +13% (regression gate triggered). Link: https://perf.redwood/team/diff/1755017890  :rotating_light:

alex: MatMulSplit +13% — probable kernel reorder fallback on one node. Anyone seen similar after the kernel selector change last week?

jamal: I saw a canary with slightly different workspace alignment that caused fallback to the non-vectorized matmul. Will bisect.

maria: I'll attach the specific trace slices and a perfetto timeline snippet for MatMulSplit to the diff card. Also added the quick repro script in the artifact that replays the same input batch shape.

sophie: Can we shrink artifact size further? zstd level 19? also store derived JSON only for PR checks to keep GH quick.

maria: Good call — GH PRs upload only metadata JSON + top-3 PNG flamegraphs. Full nsight bundle kept only for nightly and on-demand downloads.

alex: Sounds great. Next steps: jamal to bisect, maria to update selector tests, sophie to tweak retention/compression. I'll add a short doc in eng-runtime folder for ops on how to pull traces. :thumbsup:

jamal: on it, will post bisect results here.

maria: Thanks all — filing a follow-up RFC for formalizing gate thresholds and dashboard UX.

perf-bot: [scheduled job] nightly-perf-autocollect -> next run 2026-03-02T06:00:00Z
